newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA APRIL UNEMPLOYMENT RISES TO 15.3 PCT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA APRIL UNEMPLOYMENT RISES TO 15.3 PCT.

text.p: The number of people unemployed in
Bulgaria rose to 584,851 or 15.3 percent of the workforce in
April from 555,835 in March, a National Labour Exchange (NLE)
official said on Thursday.
BULGARIAN UNEMPLOYMENT APRIL MARCH APRIL'96
pct of workforce 15.3 14.5 11.0
"This is the highest unemployment rate this year so far as
demand for workforce continued to shrink due to closures of
state firms and lay-offs in the public sector," the official
who declined to be named told Reuters.
The previous high for this year was in March.
Around 55 percent of the 29,016 people registered with the
Labour Exchange in search of jobs last month had no specific
job training, 18.8 percent were higher education specialists
and 26.7 percent had a specific technical training.
Bulgaria is to close down loss-making state firms and
reduce red tape under a $657 million reform and funding
agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Under the agreement employees in the public sector are to
be cut by 58,000 by the year's end with cuts equally divided in
the last three quarters.
A total of 100,000 employees in industrial plants were also
expected to be laid off this year as a result of structural
reform, NLE preliminary estimates showed.
The World Bank has approved a $25 million loan for
severance payments and compensation for professional
retraining, and a further $80 million has been earmarked for
lending in the course of the reform.
Bulgaria's average unemployment rate for 1996 was 11.1
percent, down 0.3 points from 1995.
Unemployment peaked in January 1994, when 16.6 percent of
the workforce were jobless.
